$GRAB Ads Sept-Oct 2025 Update 🔥🔥🔥

AI SuperApp Grab Ads,  the advertising arm of Southeast Asia's leading superapp Grab, continues to demonstrate robust momentum in 2025, driven by its integration into Grab's ecosystem of mobility, deliveries, fintech, and emerging tourism services. As of Q3 2025 (ending September 30), Grab's overall advertising revenue segment reported over 100%  (YoY) growth, fueled by enhanced targeting via first-party data, AI-powered ad creation tools, and expansions in retail media networks (RMNs)

This growth persists into early October, with no major disruptions from macroeconomic factors, according to Grab COO Alex Hungate. The platform's return on ad spend (ROAS) remains a key strength, enabling brands to leverage Grab's 150+ million monthly transacting users across eight markets for online-to-offline (O2O) campaigns.

Grab Ads' evolution emphasizes self-serve tools for SMEs, hyper-localized content via generative AI (GenAI), and cross-service bundling (ads tied to rides or deliveries). Below is a month-by-month breakdown of key updates, based on earnings insights, partnerships, and platform enhancements.

Setepember + October 2025:

September marked a pivotal month for Grab Ads, with AI integrations accelerating ad efficiency and tourism-driven campaigns boosting engagement. GrabAds is the most effective in term of dollar spent from for small to large businesses.  

~AI-First Ad Tools Rollout: Grab deepened its "AI SuperApp" strategy with GenAI features for ad generation, reducing creation time by up to 99% (from 99 hours to ~90 minutes per campaign). This includes LLM-powered tools (co-developed with OpenAI and AWS) for automated content, personalization, and testing. Merchants using the AI Merchant Assistant saw 90% productivity gains in pricing and inventory optimization, directly enhancing ad performance for GrabMart and food delivery tie-ins. These tools expanded self-serve access for SMEs, targeting long-tail advertisers with sophisticated segmentation (e.g., based on real-time transaction data from rides and fintech).

~Tourism Campaign Surge: @Alipay  partnership (1.7 billion users) drove 20-25% spikes in ride frequency for tourists vs. locals, with Grab Ads capturing incremental spend via bundled promotions. In Thailand, the "Amazing Thailand Grand Tourism Year 2025" campaign (with TAT) featured celebrity-endorsed ads ( LingOrm) offering 10% off Grab services using code "AMAZING25" (valid through December). This integrated in-app banners, rewarded ads (Grab Points incentives), and OOH fleet wraps, projecting $1B-$2B in added revenue by FY2026. Similar MOUs in Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines amplified ad impressions by 15-20% through GrabMaps' location-based targeting.

~RMN and SME Focus: Enhanced Marketing Manager mobile app features allowed merchants to reserve high-visibility ad spaces in Grab-hosted campaigns, with real-time reporting and cost-per-order (CPO) pricing. A FAMA collaboration in Malaysia digitized 300+ farmers' markets, lifting SME ad-driven sales by 12-20%. GrabUnlimited perks (exclusive rebates) stacked with OpenAI's ChatGPT Plus trial (launched mid-September) increased subscriber engagement 4x, funneling more traffic to ad-supported bundles.

~GrabUnlimited and Ecosystem Ties: October promotions ( codes like "BINTON89" for discounts) layered ads into subscription perks, driving 4x higher purchase rates. Analysts project 15-20% overall revenue growth, with ads benefiting from reduced corporate costs and holiday season prep (dine-out bundles).

Higher Monthly Transacting Users will attract higher Ads revenue growth. Grab Ads' robust performance in September and October 2025 underscores its pivotal role in driving Grab's growth as Southeast Asia's leading superapp. With AI writing codes, GRAB should be able to add more attractive services that increase the MTUs significant as they expand into tourism aggressively.

Grab AI SuperApp recently launched Dine-Out , which allows users to discover, reserve tables, and access exclusive discounts at participating restaurants directly through the Grab app, continues to expand across Southeast Asia. 

Launched earlier in 2025, it's designed to boost in-restaurant dining by integrating with Grab's superapp ecosystem; no delivery fees involved, just high-margin(70-80% w/ 20-35% commission) reservations and promotions. As of early October, over 1,500 restaurants in Singapore alone are live on the platform, with similar growth in markets like Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines. ~Partnerships like Klook for 0% interest installments (4–12 months) or @Alipay w/ 1/7B users on Dine-Out + tours/attractions, aimed at tourists.

Greco Ipokrito Belgica, The Duterte Protector

Greco Belgica has once again made himself the spokesperson of confusion, posting a red-tinted statement on social media claiming that the Discayas' withdrawal from the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) investigation is because "Martin may become state witness" and that "baka sila na ang mastermind dito, ala Napoles style."

He even had the audacity to say, "Isara na ang ICI at balik na lang sa Marcoleta-led Blue Ribbon Committee hearing. Dun may tiwala ang tao."

Really, Greco? The same Blue Ribbon Committee under Marcoleta, a known Duterte ally, is where "may tiwala ang tao"? The irony is almost painful. Kung di ka ba naman tanga't bulag?

Let’s get the facts straight, the Discayas announced they will no longer participate in the ICI because cases have already been filed in court. They chose the proper legal path, a decision anchored on due process, not politics. But Belgica immediately twisted this into a smear narrative to discredit both the Discayas and former Speaker Martin Romualdez, echoing the same Duterte-style propaganda we’re witnessing everyday, accuse loudly, prove nothing, and repeat endlessly. Nakakapagod na actually, until now wala silang hawak na pruweba eh. Di ba?

What makes Belgica’s grandstanding even more hypocritical is his own record. As former chairman of the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission (PACC) under the Duterte administration, Belgica never filed a single case against Duterte allies, not even against Congressman Eric Yap, who was hounded by questions over anomalous infrastructure projects and controversial allocations. 

Yap, a loyal Duterte supporter, enjoyed complete immunity from Belgica’s so-called "anti-corruption" zeal.

Now, Belgica suddenly plays moral crusader, pretending to expose corruption while defending a rigged investigation led by Marcoleta, another Duterte loyalist. The Blue Ribbon Committee under Marcoleta has become nothing more than a political stage meant to implicate the perceived enemies of the Duterte camp, particularly Martin Romualdez.

It’s no coincidence that every time a new controversy surfaces, the Duterte propaganda network tries to drag Romualdez’s name into it. Belgica’s post is just another episode in this tired script. Apparently, when they can’t find evidence, they resort to innuendo, repetition, and insult.

I guess, for the Duterte machinery, Martin Romualdez has become the ultimate boogeyman. Every scandal, every rumor, every whisper, isisi na lang natin kay former Speaker Martin Romualdez. If there’s traffic in EDSA, if a bridge collapses, if the sky turns gray, pati lindol, it must be Martin Romualdez.

The obsession is revealing. They fear him. They know he is the strategic mind who once delivered unity and victory, the real KINGMAKER who can just as easily build a new coalition that eclipses the Duterte brand. And that’s what truly terrifies them, his capacity to lead, his political composure, and his refusal to engage in their circus.

So while Greco Ipokroto Belgica keeps posting red cards of hypocrisy and promoting a Marcoleta-led Senate Blue Ribbon Committee drama, the public is beginning to see through the act.

And that says everything.
